The thyroid is a small, butterfly-shaped gland located at the base of the front of your neck, just below the Adam’s apple. It is a critical part of your endocrine system, acting as the body's "powerhouse" by producing hormones that regulate the speed of your metabolism—how your body transforms food into energy.

Core Functions : 
The thyroid produces two primary hormones, Thyroxine (T4) and Triiodothyronine (T3), which travel through the bloodstream to affect nearly every cell in the body. These hormones control

Energy Levels: Regulating how fast you burn calories.

Vital Signs: Influencing heart rate, blood pressure, and body temperature.

Growth & Development: Crucial for brain development in infants and physical growth in children.
Digestion: Affecting how fast food moves through the digestive tract.

Common Thyroid Disorders:
Thyroid disease occurs when the gland produces too much or too little hormone, or when physical growths develop.

Hypothyroidism (Underactive): The thyroid doesn't make enough hormone, slowing down body functions. Common symptoms include fatigue, weight gain, feeling cold, and depression.

Hyperthyroidism (Overactive): The thyroid makes too much hormone, speeding up body functions. Common symptoms include weight loss (despite increased appetite), rapid heart rate, anxiety, and heat sensitivity.

Goiter: An abnormal enlargement of the gland that may look like a lump in the neck.
